Independent numerical row Fourier transform for (3,2,0.3) and numerical evaluation of the boundary constant
correctness.rationale: A same-side pair of distinct vertices has distance 2 by choosing in each q-factor an intermediate symbol different from both ends. Opposite-side pairs are at distance 1 if they differ everywhere and at distance 3 otherwise: every pair of symbols in K_q admits a length-three walk for q≥3. Thus the diagonal blocks of the powered-distance matrix are 2ᵖ(J−I), and the off-diagonal block is 3ᵖJ+(1−3ᵖ)(J_q−I_q)⊗⋯⊗(J_q−I_q). The constant and mean-zero spaces in each q-factor and the symmetric and antisymmetric spaces across sides diagonalize both blocks. The only potentially maximal centered eigenvalues for p>0 are F and −2ᵖ+M(3ᵖ−1); their real multiplicities are 1 and d(q−1). The two inequalities and strictness at p=0 follow immediately. The second multiplier has a unique positive zero after division by 2ᵖ. For the first-zero argument, a finite metric of s-negative type has strictly smaller exponents of strict negative type: realize its s-powered distances as squared Euclidean distances and use the integral for xʳ with 0<r<1 against the Gaussian kernels. On the centered subspace the integral is strictly negative for nonzero vectors, since these kernels tend to the identity at large parameter for distinct points. Hence even a first zero without a sign change cannot precede a later exponent of negative type. This verifies the stated minimum rule; the centered Gram rank gives the embedding dimensions. Finally, b₁∼1/(M log 3) and F′(0)/(Q log 3) tends to 1−(1−log 2/log 3)e^(1/α). The Taylor error on [0,b₁] is O(Nb₁²)=O(q/M)=o(1). A negative derivative stays negative for p>0; a positive limiting normalized derivative makes F(b₁)>0 eventually, with first zero asymptotic to 1/F′(0). The asymptotic boundary and both scales follow. A separate 18-character finite check at (q,d,p)=(3,2,0.3) agrees to within 6×10⁻¹⁵; the boundary constant independently evaluates to 1.0032421945194823… .
residual_risks: The floating-point check is corroborative only. The critical asymptotic regime α=α_c and unequal alphabet sizes are not classified.

value.rationale: For a natural enlargement of the crown graph, the exact endpoint and rank matter for Euclidean snowflake embeddings. The two distinct controlling eigenspaces give different rank losses, and the ratio q/d determines which loss occurs and on which scale away from its critical value. That comparison adds information beyond computing a generic distance-matrix determinant or enumerating a few graphs.
residual_risks: The transition at equality α=α_c remains open in this result.
